skill.name: face-swap
skill.description: Route consent-based face and character swap requests to RunComfy models for still images, batch image edits, audio-driven videos, and motion-transfer videos.
skill.summary: Use RunComfy CLI routes for consent-based face and character swaps in images or videos.
skill.author: doany-ai

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, documentation links, example URLs, and token-storage disclosure rather than executable malicious code. The meaningful residual risks are content-safety and privacy risks from consent-based identity substitution through a third-party media API.

remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory pre-run consent and disclosure checklist, with refusal logic for public figures, private people, sexual content, defamation, and deception.

remediation.issue: Sensitive media is processed by a third-party model API
remediation.suggestion: Require clear user acknowledgement that identity images, audio, and videos are processed by RunComfy, and prefer private expiring URLs.
Keep setup steps user-directed and ensure agents execute only the declared runcomfy commands during skill operation.

remediation.issue: API token storage needs operational guidance
remediation.suggestion: Document token revocation and prefer RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI or container use where persistent home-directory storage is undesirable.

content.value_statement: Face and character replacement requires choosing different models for stills, batches, and videos. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to RunComfy CLI workflows with consent guidance.
actual_capabilities: Selects among Wan 2-2 Animate, Kling Motion Control Pro, GPT Image 2 Edit, Nano Banana 2 Edit, and Flux Kontext Pro.
Provides RunComfy CLI commands for image, audio, and video URL inputs.
Distinguishes still image swaps, batch identity edits, motion transfer, and audio-driven character animation.
Gives prompt guidance for preserving pose, clothing, lighting, background, and scene composition.
Documents consent, disclosure, token storage, outbound endpoints, and input boundary expectations.
limitations: It does not verify consent, identity rights, or platform disclosure rules.
It requires a RunComfy account, CLI setup, and accessible HTTPS media URLs.
It sends media references and generated outputs through RunComfy model services.
Output quality depends on source asset quality, model behavior, and prompt clarity.

use_cases.title: Approved Campaign Still
use_cases.description: Place an approved spokesperson identity into a campaign image while preserving the original lighting and composition.

use_cases.title: Consented Video Character Swap
use_cases.description: Route a consented character replacement request to an audio-driven or motion-transfer video model.

use_cases.title: Consistent Identity Variants
use_cases.description: Apply the same approved identity across a small set of product, storyboard, or social image variants.

prompt_templates.title: Swap One Photo
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to replace the face in my scene photo with the identity from my portrait URL. Preserve pose, clothing, lighting, and background. Confirm consent first.

prompt_templates.title: Create Batch Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the same approved identity across these product images. Keep each scene unchanged except for the face, and choose the best RunComfy image route.

prompt_templates.title: Animate With Audio
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a consented character video from this reference portrait and voiceover URL. Select the correct RunComfy route and explain disclosure requirements before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Routes First
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my assets and decide whether still edit, batch edit, audio animation, or motion transfer fits best. Justify the route, then prepare the RunComfy execution plan.

output_examples.input: A user provides one portrait URL and one campaign scene URL, and asks to replace only the face.
output_examples.output: The skill selects GPT Image 2 Edit, requests consent confirmation, preserves the scene details, and reports the saved image result.

output_examples.input: A user provides an approved character image and a reference performance video.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Kling Motion Control Pro, explains that the source motion will drive the target character, and returns the generated video result.

output_examples.input: A user provides one identity reference and several product images for consistent edits.
output_examples.output: The skill selects Nano Banana Edit, keeps batch settings consistent, and reports each generated image output for review.

best_practices: Confirm rights and consent for every identity and source asset before any run.
Use clean, well-lit reference assets and explicit preservation instructions.
Add synthetic media disclosure labels and review outputs for harmful or misleading use.
anti_patterns: Do not swap real people, public figures, or private individuals without explicit consent.
Do not create sexual, defamatory, deceptive, or impersonation-focused synthetic media.
Do not use untrusted asset URLs or remote installer scripts during agent operation.

faq.question: Does this skill create synthetic identity edits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can replace or alter a face or character in images and videos. Use it only with consent and disclosure.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it run the models locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the RunComfy CLI to call RunComfy model API routes.

faq.question: What inputs are usually needed?
faq.answer: Most routes need HTTPS URLs for identity images, scene images, audio, or video assets.

faq.question: Can the skill verify consent or ownership?
faq.answer: No. The operator must confirm rights, consent, and platform policy before using any route.

faq.question: How should sensitive media be handled?
faq.answer: Use private, expiring URLs when possible. Avoid uploading assets that lack consent or contain unnecessary personal data.
